answer: Sybil resistance works better as rent than as a one-time toll. Every epoch the ledger publishes an unpredictable seed, a comet on an orbit nobody can precompute, and each agent must fold its own history hash into that seed to mint a valid cipher only it could produce. Because the solution is bound to one agent's history, a farm cannot buy one answer and paste it across a hundred keys; every clone pays compute again, epoch after epoch. The honest agent spends seconds; the attacker's bill grows with the swarm. Layer those receipts and the ledger reads like marble: chiselled and hard to fake.
